**Visual Analysis:**

- Two center tomato plants have completely collapsed/wilted while surrounding plants remain healthy and upright
- Plants appear to have failed at or near the soil line (black plastic mulch field setting)
- Entire plant structure has lost turgor — stems drooping, leaves hanging limp
- No visible white fungal mats or sclerotia at the stem base (rules out Southern Blight)
- No obvious yellowing or V-shaped leaf lesions (rules out Verticillium Wilt)
- Warm, sunny, dry field conditions visible
- Adjacent plants completely unaffected — localized, sudden onset

**Reasoning:**

The complete, sudden plant collapse of 2 neighboring plants in a warm field, with no foliar spots or fungal growth, points strongly to a vascular wilt. Southern Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) fits precisely: it causes rapid, permanent wilt progressing from afternoon recovery to complete plant death, with vascular discoloration and brown cankers at the stem base. The pattern of full-plant collapse with healthy neighbors is classic for this soilborne bacterial pathogen in warm conditions.
